title.zh: 卷79 列傳第44 外戚
title.raw: 卷79 列傳第44 外戚 Volume 79 Biographies 44: Imperial Affines

sentences.zh: 隋書卷七十九列傳第四十四

translations.literal: Book of Sui, Volume 79, Biographies 44
translations.idiomatic: Book of Sui, Volume 79, Biographies 44

sentences.zh: ○外戚

translations.literal: ○ Imperial Affines
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Affines

sentences.zh: 曆觀前代外戚之家，乘母后之權以取高位厚秩者多矣，然而鮮有克終之美，必罹顛覆之患，何哉？

translations.literal: Surveying the houses of imperial affines in previous ages, many rode the empress's power to obtain high rank and rich stipends, yet few enjoyed the beauty of a good end and inevitably suffered the calamity of overthrow—why?
translations.idiomatic: A survey of imperial affines in earlier dynasties shows that many used an empress's authority to win high office and rich emoluments, yet few ended well and most met ruin in the end. Why was this?

sentences.zh: 皆由乎無德而尊，不知紀極，忽于滿盈之戒，罔念高危之咎，故鬼瞰其室，憂必及之。

translations.literal: All were because, honored without virtue, they did not know the limits of propriety, neglected the warning of fullness and overflow, and gave no thought to the blame of standing in perilous height; therefore ghosts peered into their houses, and sorrow was bound to reach them.
translations.idiomatic: They were honored without merit, knew no bounds, ignored the warning that fullness invites spillover, and forgot how dangerous it is to stand too high—so malign forces watched their households, and disaster was sure to follow.

sentences.zh: 夫其誠著艱難，功宣社稷，不以謙沖自牧，未免顛蹶之禍，而況道不足以濟時，仁不足以利物，自矜於己，以富貴驕人者乎？

translations.literal: As for those whose sincerity shone in hardship and whose merit was proclaimed to the altars of state, if they did not cultivate themselves with modesty and restraint, they still could not escape the calamity of a fall—how much more those whose Way was insufficient to rescue the age, whose benevolence was insufficient to benefit things, who prided themselves and used wealth and rank to insult others?
translations.idiomatic: Even men whose loyalty had been proved in adversity and whose service to the state was real, if they did not govern themselves with humility, could not escape ruin—how much less those whose conduct could not save the times, whose kindness could not help others, yet who flaunted their own worth and lorded their wealth over everyone?

sentences.zh: 此呂、霍、上官、閻、梁、竇、鄧所以繼踵而亡滅者也。

translations.literal: This is why the Lü, Huo, Shangguan, Yan, Liang, Dou, and Deng clans followed one another in succession yet perished and were extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: This is why the houses of Lü, Huo, Shangguan, Yan, Liang, Dou, and Deng rose one after another only to be destroyed in turn.

sentences.zh: 昔文皇潛躍之際，獻後便相推轂，煬帝大橫方兆，蕭妃密勿經綸，是以恩禮綢繆，始終不易。

translations.literal: Formerly, when Emperor Wen was still rising in obscurity, Empress Xian already pushed the carriage wheel for him; when Emperor Yang's great mandate was just appearing, Consort Xiao secretly labored in statecraft—therefore favor and ritual courtesies were thickly woven and never changed from beginning to end.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen was still making his way to power, Empress Xian already stood at his side; when Emperor Yang's reign was taking shape, Consort Xiao worked closely on affairs of state. Favor and ceremony were therefore constant and unwavering throughout.

sentences.zh: 然內外親戚，莫預朝權，昆弟在位，亦無殊寵。

translations.literal: Yet among inner and outer kin by marriage, none took part in court power; brothers in office likewise received no special favor.
translations.idiomatic: Yet none of their affinal kin, whether close or distant, held real power at court, and even brothers who held office received no extraordinary privilege.

sentences.zh: 至於居擅玉堂，家稱金穴，暉光戚裡，重灼四方，將三司以比儀，命五侯而同拜者，終始一代，寂無聞焉。

translations.literal: As for those who monopolized the jade hall, whose households were called golden caves, whose brilliance lit the imperial affines' quarter and whose weight scorched the four quarters, who were matched in ceremony with the Three Excellencies and ordered the Five Marquises to bow together with them—throughout a whole generation, not a sound was heard of such things.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the dynasty one heard nothing of affines who seized the halls of government, whose houses were proverbial treasure vaults, whose splendor dazzled the whole clan and whose influence blazed across the realm, who were treated like the Three Excellencies or who had the Five Marquises bow with them.

sentences.zh: 考之前王，可謂矯其弊矣。

translations.literal: Comparing with former kings, it may be said that they corrected this abuse.
translations.idiomatic: Measured against earlier rulers, the Sui emperors may be said to have corrected this longstanding abuse.

sentences.zh: 故雖時經擾攘，無有陷於不義，市朝遷貿，而皆得以保全。

translations.literal: Therefore, although the times passed through turmoil, none fell into injustice; though markets and courts shifted and changed, all were able to be preserved intact.
translations.idiomatic: Thus even when the realm was in turmoil, none of these kin were drawn into wrongful ruin, and though power shifted in the capital, they were able to survive.

sentences.zh: 比夫憑藉寵私，階緣恩澤，乘其非據，旋就顛隕者，豈可同日而言哉！

translations.literal: Compared with those who relied on private favor, climbed by grace and bounty, seized what was not theirs to hold, and promptly met overturn and ruin—how can they be spoken of on the same day!
translations.idiomatic: How can they be compared with those who traded on private favor, climbed by imperial indulgence, seized what they had no right to hold, and were soon destroyed?

sentences.zh: 此所謂愛之以禮，能改覆車。

translations.literal: This is what is called loving them with ritual propriety and being able to change the overturned cart.
translations.idiomatic: This is what it means to love them with proper restraint and to keep them from repeating the disasters of the past.

sentences.zh: 輒敘其事，為《外戚傳》雲。

translations.literal: I therefore narrate these affairs and make them the 'Biographies of Imperial Affines.'
translations.idiomatic: I therefore set out these accounts in the 'Biographies of Imperial Affines.'

sentences.zh: ○高祖外家呂氏

translations.literal: ○ The Lü Clan, Maternal Kin of Emperor Gaozu
translations.idiomatic: The Lü Clan, Maternal Kin of Emperor Gaozu

sentences.zh: 高祖外家呂氏，其族蓋微，平齊之後，求訪不知所在。

translations.literal: The Lü clan, maternal kin of Emperor Gaozu—their lineage was quite humble. After the pacification of Qi, searches were made but their whereabouts were unknown.
translations.idiomatic: The Lü clan on Emperor Gaozu's mother's side was of humble origin. After the conquest of Qi, officials searched for them but could not find where they lived.

sentences.zh: 至開皇初，濟南郡上言，有男子呂永吉，自稱有姑字苦桃，為楊忠妻。

translations.literal: By the beginning of the Kaihuang era, Jinan commandery reported that a man named Lü Yongji claimed to have an aunt styled Kutao who had been the wife of Yang Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaihuang reign, Jinan commandery reported that a man named Lü Yongji claimed an aunt called Kutao had been the wife of Yang Zhong.

sentences.zh: 勘驗知是舅子，始追贈外祖雙周為上柱國、太尉、八州諸軍事、青州刺史，封齊郡公，諡曰敬，外祖母姚氏為齊敬公夫人。

translations.literal: On investigation it was known that he was a nephew by the maternal line; only then were posthumous honors granted to the maternal grandfather Shuangzhou as Pillar of the State of the First Rank, Grand Commandant, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in Eight Provinces, and Governor of Qing Province, enfeoffed as Duke of Qi commandery with the posthumous title Jing; the maternal grandmother, the Yao clan, was made Lady of Duke Jing of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Investigation confirmed he was a maternal nephew. The court then posthumously honored the maternal grandfather Shuangzhou as Pillar of the State of the First Rank, Grand Commandant, commander of military affairs in eight provinces, and Governor of Qing Province, enfeoffed him as Duke of Qi with the posthumous title Jing, and styled the maternal grandmother, Lady Yao, consort of Duke Jing of Qi.

sentences.zh: 詔並改葬，于齊州立廟，置守塚十家。

translations.literal: An edict ordered them all reburied, a temple established in Qi province, and ten households appointed to guard the tombs.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered new burials, a temple built in Qi province, and ten households assigned to tend the graves.

sentences.zh: 以永吉襲爵，留在京師。

translations.literal: Yongji was made to inherit the title and was kept in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yongji inherited the title and remained in the capital.

sentences.zh: 大業中，授上党郡太守，性識庸劣，職務不理。

translations.literal: During the Daye era he was appointed Administrator of Shangdang commandery; his nature and understanding were mediocre and inferior, and he did not manage his duties.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye reign he was made Administrator of Shangdang commandery, but his abilities were poor and he neglected his office.

sentences.zh: 後去官，不知所終。

translations.literal: Later he left office; his end is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: He later left office, and nothing further is known of him.

sentences.zh: 永吉從父道貴，性尤頑騃，言詞鄙陋。

translations.literal: Yongji's paternal cousin Daogui was by nature especially dull and stupid, and his words were coarse and vulgar.
translations.idiomatic: Yongji's cousin Daogui was exceptionally dull-witted and spoke in crude, vulgar language.

sentences.zh: 初自鄉里征入長安，上見之悲泣。

translations.literal: When he was first summoned from the countryside to Chang'an, upon seeing him the emperor wept in grief.
translations.idiomatic: When he was first summoned from the countryside to Chang'an, the emperor wept at the sight of him.

sentences.zh: 道貴略無戚容，但連呼高祖名，雲：「種末定不可偷，大似苦桃姊。

translations.literal: Daogui showed hardly any sorrowful expression but only repeatedly called the emperor by his personal name, saying, 'The seed is not yet fixed and cannot be stolen—it greatly resembles Elder Sister Kutao.'
translations.idiomatic: Daogui showed little grief and kept calling the emperor by his personal name, saying, 'The breed isn't settled yet—you can't cheat that. You look just like Elder Sister Kutao.'

sentences.zh: 」是後數犯忌諱，動致違忤，上甚耽之。

translations.literal: ' Thereafter he repeatedly violated taboos and constantly caused offense; the emperor was greatly wearied of him.
translations.idiomatic: After that he repeatedly broke taboos and gave offense, and the emperor grew thoroughly weary of him.

sentences.zh: 乃命高熲厚加供給，不許接對朝士。

translations.literal: The emperor then ordered Gao Jiong to supply him generously but not permit him to meet and converse with court officials.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Gao Jiong to provide for him generously but forbade him to associate with court officials.

sentences.zh: 拜上儀同三司，出為濟南太守，令即之任，斷其入朝。

translations.literal: He was appointed Senior Master of Uniformity of the Third Rank, sent out as Administrator of Jinan, ordered to proceed at once to his post, and cut off from entering court.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Senior Master of Uniformity of the Third Rank and sent out as Administrator of Jinan with orders to take up his post immediately and never return to court.

sentences.zh: 道貴還至本郡，高自崇重，每與人言，自稱皇舅。

translations.literal: Daogui returned to his home commandery, held himself high in self-esteem, and in speaking with people always called himself the emperor's maternal uncle.
translations.idiomatic: Back in his home commandery, Daogui held himself in high esteem and told everyone he met that he was the emperor's maternal uncle.

sentences.zh: 數將儀衛出入閭裡，從故人游宴，官民鹹苦之。

translations.literal: He often led guards of honor in and out of the lanes and alleys, followed old acquaintances in feasting and drinking, and officials and commoners alike suffered from it.
translations.idiomatic: He often paraded with an armed escort through the streets, caroused with old friends, and officials and commoners alike resented him.

sentences.zh: 後郡廢，終於家，子孫無聞焉。

translations.literal: Later the commandery was abolished; he ended his life at home, and nothing was heard of his descendants.
translations.idiomatic: When the commandery was later abolished, he died at home, and nothing more is recorded of his descendants.

sentences.zh: 獨孤羅弟陀

translations.literal: Dugu Luo and His Younger Brother Tuo
translations.idiomatic: Dugu Luo and His Younger Brother Tuo

sentences.zh: 獨孤羅，字羅仁，雲中人也。

translations.literal: Dugu Luo, styled Luoren, was a native of Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Dugu Luo, styled Luoren, was a native of Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 父信，初仕魏為荊州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Xin at first served Wei as Governor of Jing province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xin first served Northern Wei as Governor of Jing province.

sentences.zh: 武帝之入關也，信棄父母妻子西歸長安，曆職顯貴，羅由是遂為高氏所囚。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu entered the Pass, Xin abandoned his parents, wife, and children and returned west to Chang'an, passing through offices of eminent nobility; because of this Luo was then imprisoned by the Gao clan.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou entered the Pass, Xin abandoned his parents, wife, and children and went west to Chang'an, where he rose to high office. Luo was left behind and imprisoned by the Gao clan of Northern Qi.

sentences.zh: 信後仕周為大司馬。

translations.literal: Xin later served Zhou as Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Xin later served Northern Zhou as Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 及信為宇文護所誅，羅始見釋，寓居中山，孤貧無以自給。

translations.literal: When Xin was executed by Yuwen Hu, Luo was only then released, lodged in Zhongshan, and was orphaned and poor with no means to support himself.
translations.idiomatic: After Xin was executed by Yuwen Hu, Luo was finally released. He lived in Zhongshan, alone and destitute, with no means to support himself.

sentences.zh: 齊將獨孤永業以宗族之故，見而哀之，為買田宅，遺以資畜。

translations.literal: The Qi general Dugu Yongye, because of clan ties, saw him and pitied him, bought fields and a house for him, and gave him livestock and goods.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Qi general Dugu Yongye, a kinsman, took pity on him, bought him land and a house, and gave him livestock and supplies.

sentences.zh: 初，信入關之後，複娶二妻，郭氏生子六人，善、穆、藏、順、陀、整，崔氏生獻皇后。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Xin entered the Pass, he took two wives again: the Guo clan bore six sons—Shan, Mu, Zang, Shun, Tuo, and Zheng; the Cui clan bore Empress Xian.
translations.idiomatic: After Xin entered the Pass he had taken two more wives. Lady Guo bore six sons—Shan, Mu, Zang, Shun, Tuo, and Zheng—and Lady Cui bore Empress Xian.

sentences.zh: 及齊亡，高祖為定州總管，獻皇后遣人尋羅，得之，相見悲不自勝，侍御者皆泣。

translations.literal: When Qi perished, Emperor Gaozu was Governor-General of Ding province; Empress Xian sent men to seek Luo, found him, and upon meeting grieved beyond control—all who attended wept.
translations.idiomatic: After Qi fell, while Gaozu was Governor-General of Ding province, Empress Xian sent men to find Luo. When they met, grief overwhelmed them and all who were present wept.

sentences.zh: 於是厚遺車馬財物。

translations.literal: Thereupon she generously sent carriages, horses, and goods.
translations.idiomatic: She then sent him generous gifts of carriages, horses, and goods.

sentences.zh: 未幾，周武帝以羅功臣子，久淪異域，征拜楚安郡太守。

translations.literal: Before long, Emperor Wu of Zhou, because Luo was the son of a meritorious minister long lost in a foreign land, summoned and appointed him Administrator of Chu'an commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Emperor Wu of Zhou, noting that Luo was the son of a meritorious minister long stranded in enemy territory, appointed him Administrator of Chu'an commandery.

sentences.zh: 以疾去官，歸於京師。

translations.literal: Because of illness he left office and returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Illness forced him to leave office, and he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 諸弟見羅少長貧賤，每輕侮之，不以兄禮事也。

translations.literal: His younger brothers, seeing that Luo had from youth grown up in poverty and low station, always treated him lightly and insultingly and did not serve him with the rites due an elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brothers, knowing he had grown up poor and far away, often slighted him and did not treat him with proper respect as their elder brother.

sentences.zh: 然性長者，亦不與諸弟校競長短，後由是重之。

translations.literal: Yet by nature he was a man of forbearance and did not compete with his younger brothers over who was greater or lesser; afterward for this reason they came to respect him.
translations.idiomatic: But Luo was by nature forbearing and did not quarrel with them over precedence, and in time they came to respect him for it.

sentences.zh: 及高祖為丞相，拜儀同，常置左右。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu became Chancellor, Luo was appointed Master of Uniformity and constantly kept at his side.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu became Chancellor, Luo was made Master of Uniformity and kept constantly at his side.

sentences.zh: 既受禪，下詔追贈羅父信官爵曰：「褒德累行，往代通規，追遠慎終，前王盛典。

translations.literal: After he received the abdication, an edict was issued to posthumously grant offices and titles to Luo's father Xin, saying: 'Honoring virtue and heaping up conduct is the common rule of past ages; pursuing the distant and being careful at the end is the great ceremony of former kings.'
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozu took the throne, he issued an edict posthumously honoring Luo's father Xin: 'To reward virtue and accumulated merit is the constant practice of former ages; to honor the dead and see their rites through is the great duty of ancient kings.'

sentences.zh: 故柱國信，風宇高曠，獨秀生民，睿哲居宗，清猷映世。

translations.literal: 'The former Pillar of the State Xin had bearing lofty and spacious, standing alone in excellence among the people; sagely wisdom dwelt in the clan ancestor; pure plans shone upon the age.'
translations.idiomatic: 'The late Pillar of the State Xin bore himself with lofty dignity and stood apart among men; his wisdom illuminated the clan and his clear counsel shone upon the age.'

sentences.zh: 宏謀長策，道著於弼諧，緯義經仁，事深於拯濟。

translations.literal: 'Grand designs and far-reaching policies—his Way was manifest in assisting and harmonizing; weaving righteousness and threading benevolence—his affairs went deep into rescue and relief.'
translations.idiomatic: 'His great plans and long counsel guided the state; in weaving righteousness and ordering benevolence his work went deep into saving the realm.'

sentences.zh: 方當宣風廊廟，亮采臺階，而運屬艱危，功高弗賞，眷言令範，事切於心。

translations.literal: 'Just as he was about to spread the wind of reform in the hall of state and display his colors on the terrace steps, fortune met with hardship and peril; his merit was high yet went unrewarded—recalling his fine model, the matter cuts to the heart.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Just as he was to bring his influence to the court and serve at the highest level, fate turned harsh; his merit went unrewarded, and remembering his example moves the heart.'

sentences.zh: 今景運初開，椒闈肅建，載懷塗山之義，無忘褒、紀之典。

translations.literal: 'Now as the bright fortune first opens and the pepper chambers are solemnly established, bearing in mind the righteousness of Mount Tu, let us not forget the ceremonies of Bao and Ji.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Now, as a new reign begins and the inner palace is duly established, mindful of the duty owed to a consort's kin, let us not forget the honors due to the fathers of empresses.'

sentences.zh: 可贈太師、上柱國、冀定等十州刺史、趙國公，邑萬戶。

translations.literal: 'He may be posthumously granted Grand Preceptor, Pillar of the State of the First Rank, Governor of ten provinces including Ji and Ding, and Duke of Zhao state with a fief of ten thousand households.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Let him be posthumously made Grand Preceptor, Pillar of the State of the First Rank, nominal governor of ten provinces including Ji and Ding, and Duke of Zhao with a fief of ten thousand households.'

sentences.zh: 」其諸弟以羅母沒齊，先無夫人之號，不當承襲。

translations.literal: ' His younger brothers, because Luo's mother had died in Qi and had never borne the title of Lady, ought not to inherit.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brothers argued that because Luo's mother had died in Qi and had never held the title of Lady, he ought not to inherit the title.

sentences.zh: 上以問後，後曰：「羅誠嫡長，不可誣也。

translations.literal: The emperor asked the empress; the empress said, 'Luo is truly the eldest son of the principal wife—this cannot be falsified.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked the empress, who replied, 'Luo is truly the eldest son of the principal line—this cannot be denied.'

sentences.zh: 」於是襲爵趙國公。

translations.literal: ' Thereupon he inherited the title of Duke of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Luo therefore inherited the title of Duke of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 以其弟善為河內郡公，穆為金泉縣公，藏為武平縣公，陀為武喜縣公，整為千牛備身。

translations.literal: His younger brother Shan was made Duke of Henei commandery, Mu Duke of Jinquan county, Zang Duke of Wuping county, Tuo Duke of Wuxi county, and Zheng an attendant of the Thousand-Ox Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Shan was made Duke of Henei commandery, Mu Duke of Jinquan county, Zang Duke of Wuping county, Tuo Duke of Wuxi county, and Zheng an attendant of the Thousand-Ox Guard.

sentences.zh: 擢拜羅為左領左右將軍，尋遷左衛將軍，前後賞賜不可勝計。

translations.literal: Luo was promoted and appointed General of the Left Guard of the Left and Right, soon transferred to General of the Left Guard, and rewards before and after were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Luo was promoted to General of the Left Guard of the Left and Right, soon made General of the Left Guard, and received rewards beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 久而出為涼州總管，進位上柱國。

translations.literal: After a long time he went out as Governor-General of Liang province and advanced to Pillar of the State of the First Rank.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was sent out as Governor-General of Liang province and advanced to Pillar of the State of the First Rank.

sentences.zh: 仁壽中，征拜左武衛大將軍。

translations.literal: During the Renshou era he was summoned and appointed Grand General of the Left Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: During the Renshou era he was recalled and made Grand General of the Left Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，改封蜀國公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, Luo's enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Shu state.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, Luo's title was changed to Duke of Shu.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒官，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: Before long he died in office; his posthumous title was Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died in office and was given the posthumous title Gong.

sentences.zh: 子纂嗣，仕至河陽郡尉。

translations.literal: His son Zuan inherited the title and served up to Commandant of Heyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zuan inherited the title and rose to Commandant of Heyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 纂弟武都，大業末，亦為河陽郡尉。

translations.literal: Zuan's younger brother Wudu, at the end of the Daye era, also became Commandant of Heyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan's younger brother Wudu also became Commandant of Heyang commandery late in the Daye reign.

sentences.zh: 庶長子開遠，宇文化及之弑逆也，裴虔通率賊入成象殿，宿衛兵士皆從逆，開遠時為千牛，與獨孤盛力戰於閤下，為賊所執，賊義而舍之。

translations.literal: The eldest son by a concubine, Kaiyuan—when Yuwen Huaji committed regicide, Pei Qiantong led rebels into Chengxian Hall; the palace guards all followed the rebels. Kaiyuan was then in the Thousand-Ox Guard; he and Dugu Sheng fought fiercely below the gate-tower, were seized by the rebels, and the rebels, moved by righteousness, released them.
translations.idiomatic: A concubine's eldest son, Kaiyuan: when Yuwen Huaji murdered the emperor, Pei Qiantong led the rebels into Chengxian Hall and the palace guards joined them. Kaiyuan was then in the Thousand-Ox Guard. He and Dugu Sheng fought fiercely at the gate, were captured, but the rebels, admiring their courage, let them go.

sentences.zh: 善後官至柱國。

translations.literal: Shan later reached the office of Pillar of the State.
translations.idiomatic: Shan later rose to Pillar of the State.

sentences.zh: 卒，子覽嗣，仕至左候衛將軍，大業末卒。

translations.literal: He died; his son Lan inherited the title, served up to General of the Left Garrison Guard, and died at the end of the Daye era.
translations.idiomatic: He died. His son Lan inherited the title, rose to General of the Left Garrison Guard, and died late in the Daye reign.

sentences.zh: 獨孤陀，字黎邪。

translations.literal: Dugu Tuo, styled Lixie.
translations.idiomatic: Dugu Tuo, styled Lixie.

sentences.zh: 仕周胥附上士，坐父徙蜀郡十餘年。

translations.literal: He served Zhou as a gentleman-attendant of Xufu and, because of his father, was banished to Shu commandery for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: He served Northern Zhou as a gentleman-attendant of Xufu and, because of his father's fate, was exiled to Shu commandery for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 宇文護被誅，始歸長安。

translations.literal: When Yuwen Hu was executed, he only then returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuwen Hu was executed, he was able to return to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，拜上開府、右領左右將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu received the abdication, Tuo was appointed Senior Opener of the Government and General of the Right Guard of the Left and Right.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, Tuo was made Senior Opener of the Government and General of the Right Guard of the Left and Right.

sentences.zh: 久之，出為郢州刺史，進位上大將軍，累轉延州刺史。

translations.literal: After a long time he went out as Governor of E province, advanced to Grand General of the Upper Rank, and was repeatedly transferred to Governor of Yan province.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was sent out as Governor of E province, advanced to Grand General of the Upper Rank, and later transferred to Governor of Yan province.

sentences.zh: 好左道。

translations.literal: He was fond of heterodox ways.
translations.idiomatic: He was devoted to heterodox cult practices.

sentences.zh: 其妻母先事貓鬼，因轉入其家。

translations.literal: His wife's mother had first served the cat-demon, and the practice therefore passed into his household.
translations.idiomatic: His wife's mother had first practiced the cat-demon cult, and the rite passed into his household.

sentences.zh: 上微聞而不之信也。

translations.literal: The emperor heard a little of it but did not believe it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had heard rumors but did not believe them.

sentences.zh: 會獻皇后及楊素妻鄭氏俱有疾，召醫者視之，皆曰：「此貓鬼疾也。

translations.literal: It happened that both Empress Xian and Yang Su's wife, the Zheng clan, were ill; physicians were summoned to examine them, and all said, 'This is cat-demon sickness.'
translations.idiomatic: When both Empress Xian and Yang Su's wife Lady Zheng fell ill, physicians were called and all said, 'This is cat-demon sickness.'

sentences.zh: 」上以陀後之異母弟，陀妻楊素之異母妹，由是意陀所為，陰令其兄穆以情喻之。

translations.literal: ' The emperor, because Tuo was the empress's younger half-brother and Tuo's wife was Yang Su's younger half-sister, therefore suspected Tuo's doing and secretly ordered his elder brother Mu to explain the situation to him by feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Because Tuo was the empress's younger half-brother and his wife was Yang Su's younger half-sister, the emperor suspected Tuo and secretly had his brother Mu reason with him.

sentences.zh: 上又避左右諷陀，陀言無有。

translations.literal: The emperor also, avoiding those at his side, admonished Tuo indirectly; Tuo said there was nothing of the kind.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also spoke to Tuo privately and hinted at his suspicions, but Tuo denied everything.

sentences.zh: 上不悅，左轉遷州刺史。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased and transferred him to the left as Governor of Qian province.
translations.idiomatic: Displeased, the emperor demoted him to Governor of Qian province.

sentences.zh: 出怨言。

translations.literal: He uttered resentful words.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke resentfully of his treatment.

sentences.zh: 上令左僕射高熲、納言蘇威、大理正皇甫孝緒、大理丞楊遠等雜治之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Left Vice Director Gao Jiong, Admonisher Su Wei, Chief Judge of the Court of Judicial Review Huangfu Xiaoxu, Assistant Judge Yang Yuan, and others jointly to try the case.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Left Vice Director Gao Jiong, Admonisher Su Wei, Chief Judge Huangfu Xiaoxu, Assistant Judge Yang Yuan, and others to investigate jointly.

sentences.zh: 陀婢徐阿尼言，本從陀母家來，常事貓鬼。

translations.literal: Tuo's maid Xu Ani testified that she had originally come from Tuo's mother's household and had constantly served the cat-demon.
translations.idiomatic: Tuo's maid Xu Ani testified that she had come from his mother's household and had long served the cat-demon.

sentences.zh: 每以子日夜祀之。

translations.literal: Every night at the hour of zi she sacrificed to it.
translations.idiomatic: Every night at the hour of zi she made offerings to it.

sentences.zh: 言子者鼠也。

translations.literal: 'Saying zi means the rat.'
translations.idiomatic: By 'zi' she meant the rat—the hour of the rat.

sentences.zh: 其貓鬼每殺人者，所死家財物潛移於畜貓鬼家。

translations.literal: Whenever the cat-demon killed someone, the wealth and goods of the dead household were secretly transferred to the household that kept the cat-demon.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the cat-demon killed someone, the victim's wealth was secretly transferred to the household that kept the demon.

sentences.zh: 陀嘗從家中素酒，其妻曰：「無錢可酤。

translations.literal: Tuo once asked for plain wine from the household stores; his wife said, 'There is no money to buy any.'
translations.idiomatic: Tuo once asked for wine from the household stores. His wife said, 'We have no money to buy any.'

sentences.zh: 」陀因謂阿尼曰：「可令貓鬼向越公家，使我足錢也。

translations.literal: ' Tuo thereupon said to Ani, 'You can make the cat-demon go to the Duke of Yue's household so that I have enough money.'
translations.idiomatic: Tuo then told Ani, 'Send the cat-demon to the Duke of Yue's house so we'll have enough money.'

sentences.zh: 」阿尼便咒之歸。

translations.literal: ' Ani then chanted to send it back.
translations.idiomatic: Ani chanted the spell to send it.

sentences.zh: 數日，貓鬼向素家。

translations.literal: Within several days the cat-demon turned toward the Su household.
translations.idiomatic: Within days the cat-demon was directed at Yang Su's household.

sentences.zh: 十一年，上初從并州還，陀於園中謂阿尼曰：「可令貓鬼向皇后所，使多賜吾物。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, when the emperor had just returned from Bing province, Tuo said to Ani in the garden, 'You can make the cat-demon go to where the empress is so that she bestows many things on me.'
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, soon after the emperor returned from Bing province, Tuo told Ani in the garden, 'Send the cat-demon to the empress's quarters so she will give me many gifts.'

sentences.zh: 」阿尼複咒之，遂入宮中。

translations.literal: ' Ani again chanted, and it thereupon entered the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Ani chanted again, and the demon entered the palace.

sentences.zh: 楊遠乃于門下外省遣阿尼呼貓鬼。

translations.literal: Yang Yuan then, at the Outer Office of the Gate Department, sent Ani to summon the cat-demon.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yuan then had Ani summon the cat-demon at the Outer Office of the Gate Department.

sentences.zh: 阿尼於是夜中置香粥一盆，以匙扣而呼之曰：「貓女可來，無住宮中。

translations.literal: Ani then at night placed a basin of fragrant porridge, knocked with a spoon, and called out, 'Cat-girl, you may come—do not stay in the palace.'
translations.idiomatic: That night Ani set out a basin of fragrant porridge, tapped it with a spoon, and called, 'Cat-girl, come—but do not stay in the palace.'

sentences.zh: 」久之，阿尼色正青，若被牽曳者，雲貓鬼已至。

translations.literal: ' After a long while Ani's complexion turned pure blue, as if she were being dragged and pulled, and she said the cat-demon had arrived.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while Ani's face turned blue, as if she were being pulled, and she said the cat-demon had come.

sentences.zh: 上以其事下公卿，奇章公牛弘曰：「妖由人興，殺其人可以絕矣。

translations.literal: The emperor submitted the matter to the high ministers; Niuzhang Gong Niu Hong said, 'Omens arise through people—kill the person and it can be cut off.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor referred the case to the high ministers. Niu Hong of Niuzhang said, 'Such evil arises through people—execute the culprit and it will end.'

sentences.zh: 」上令以犢車載陀夫妻，將賜死於其家。

translations.literal: ' The emperor ordered Tuo and his wife loaded on a calf cart and was about to grant them death at their home.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Tuo and his wife placed on a cart and sent to their home to be executed.

sentences.zh: 陀弟司勳侍中整詣闕求哀，於是免陀死，除名為民，以其妻楊氏為尼。

translations.literal: Tuo's younger brother Zheng, Attendant at the Palace Secretariat in the Bureau of Merit, went to the palace gate to beg for mercy; thereupon Tuo's death was remitted, his name was struck off and he was made a commoner, and his wife, the Yang clan, was made a nun.
translations.idiomatic: Tuo's brother Zheng, Attendant at the Palace Secretariat in the Bureau of Merit, pleaded at court for mercy. Tuo's death sentence was remitted; he was stripped of rank and made a commoner, and his wife Lady Yang was forced to become a nun.

sentences.zh: 先是，有人訟其母為人貓鬼所殺者，上以為妖妄，怒而遣之。

translations.literal: Earlier, someone had sued, claiming his mother had been killed by someone's cat-demon; the emperor regarded it as demonic delusion, grew angry, and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, a man had sued, claiming his mother had been killed by someone's cat-demon. The emperor dismissed it as superstitious nonsense and angrily sent him away.

sentences.zh: 及此，詔誅被訟行貓鬼家。

translations.literal: At this point an edict ordered the execution of the household accused of practicing the cat-demon that had been sued.
translations.idiomatic: Now an edict ordered the household accused in that earlier suit, who practiced the cat-demon cult, put to death.

sentences.zh: 經未幾而卒。

translations.literal: Not long after, Tuo died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Tuo died.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，追念舅氏，聽以禮葬，乃下詔曰：「外氏衰禍，獨孤陀不幸早世，遷卜有期。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang took the throne, recalling his maternal kin, he permitted burial according to ritual and issued an edict saying, 'The maternal clan has met with decline and calamity; Dugu Tuo, unhappily, died young, and the time for moving the tomb is fixed.'
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang took the throne, mindful of his mother's kin, he allowed Tuo a proper burial and issued an edict: 'Our maternal clan has suffered decline; Dugu Tuo died young, and the time to move his tomb is at hand.'

sentences.zh: 言念渭陽之情，追懷傷切，宜加禮命，允備哀榮。

translations.literal: Speaking of the feeling of Weiyang, recalling with grief and pain, ritual honors should be added and full mourning glory granted.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of kinship ties, deeply grieved at his loss, let him receive posthumous honors worthy of full mourning and glory.

sentences.zh: 可贈正議大夫。

translations.literal: He may be posthumously granted Grand Master of Correct Discussion.
translations.idiomatic: Let him be posthumously made Grand Master of Correct Discussion.

sentences.zh: 」帝意猶不已，複下詔曰：「舅氏之尊，戚屬斯重，而降年弗永，凋落相繼。

translations.literal: ' The emperor's feelings were still not satisfied, and he again issued an edict saying, 'The honor due maternal uncles, the weight of affinal kin—yet their allotted years are not long, and withering and falling follow one another.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's grief was still not satisfied, and he issued another edict: 'Maternal uncles are kin of the highest honor, yet their years are brief, and one after another they fall away.'

sentences.zh: 緬惟先往，宜崇徽秩。

translations.literal: Looking back to those who went before, their eminent ranks should be exalted.
translations.idiomatic: Remembering those who have gone before, let their ranks be raised in honor.

sentences.zh: 複贈銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was again posthumously granted Grand Master of the Palace with Silver-Green Tether.
translations.idiomatic: Tuo was again posthumously made Grand Master of the Palace with Silver-Green Tether.

sentences.zh: 」有二子：延福、延壽。

translations.literal: ' He had two sons: Yanfu and Yanshou.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Yanfu and Yanshou.

sentences.zh: 陀弟整，官至幽州刺史，大業初卒，贈金紫光祿大夫，平鄉侯。

translations.literal: Tuo's younger brother Zheng reached the office of Governor of You province; he died at the beginning of the Daye era and was posthumously granted Grand Master of the Palace with Gold-Purple Tether and made Marquis of Pingxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Tuo's brother Zheng rose to Governor of You province, died early in the Daye reign, and was posthumously made Grand Master of the Palace with Gold-Purple Tether and Marquis of Pingxiang.

sentences.zh: 蕭巋子琮琮弟瓛

translations.literal: Xiao Kui's Son Cong and Cong's Younger Brother Huan
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Kui's Son Cong and Cong's Younger Brother Huan

sentences.zh: 蕭巋，字仁遠，梁昭明太子統之孫也。

translations.literal: Xiao Kui, styled Renyuan, was a grandson of Liang's Crown Prince Zhaoming, Tong.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Kui, styled Renyuan, was a grandson of Liang Crown Prince Zhaoming, Xiao Tong.

sentences.zh: 父詧，初封岳陽王，鎮襄陽。

translations.literal: His father Cha was at first enfeoffed as Prince of Yueyang and garrisoned Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Cha was first enfeoffed as Prince of Yueyang and stationed at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，其兄河東王譽與其叔父湘東王繹不協，為繹所害。

translations.literal: During Hou Jing's rebellion, his elder brother the Prince of Hedong, Yu, was at odds with his uncle the Prince of Xiangdong, Yi, and was killed by Yi.
translations.idiomatic: During Hou Jing's rebellion, his elder brother Prince Yu of Hedong fell out with their uncle Prince Yi of Xiangdong, who had him killed.

sentences.zh: 及繹嗣位，詧稱籓於西魏，乞師請討繹。

translations.literal: When Yi succeeded to the throne, Cha declared himself a vassal of Western Wei, begged for troops, and requested an expedition against Yi.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi took the throne, Cha submitted to Western Wei as a vassal, asked for troops, and sought to attack Yi.

sentences.zh: 周太祖以詧為梁主，遣柱國於謹等率騎五萬襲繹，滅之。

translations.literal: Grand Ancestor of Zhou made Cha ruler of Liang and sent the Pillar of the State Yu Jin and others leading fifty thousand horsemen to strike Yi and destroy him.
translations.idiomatic: The founder of Northern Zhou installed Cha as ruler of Liang and sent the Pillar of the State Yu Jin with fifty thousand cavalry to attack and destroy Yi.

sentences.zh: 詧遂都江陵，有荊郡、其西平州延袤三百里之地，稱皇帝于其國，車服節文一同王者。

translations.literal: Cha then moved the capital to Jiangling, held Jing commandery and Xiping province stretching three hundred li in length and breadth, styled himself emperor in his state, and his carriages, robes, and ritual regulations were all the same as a king's.
translations.idiomatic: Cha moved his capital to Jiangling, held Jing commandery and Xiping province—some three hundred li in extent—and proclaimed himself emperor. His carriages, dress, and ritual matched those of a sovereign.

sentences.zh: 仍置江陵總管，以兵戍之。

translations.literal: A Governor-General of Jiangling was still established to garrison it with troops.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Zhou still stationed a Governor-General at Jiangling with troops to guard the region.

sentences.zh: 詧薨，巋嗣位，年號天保。

translations.literal: When Cha died, Kui succeeded to the throne; his era name was Tianbao.
translations.idiomatic: After Cha died, Kui succeeded him and took the era name Tianbao.

sentences.zh: 巋俊辯有才學，兼好內典。

translations.literal: Kui was handsome, eloquent, and possessed learning; he also loved Buddhist scriptures.
translations.idiomatic: Kui was handsome, eloquent, and learned, and he also loved Buddhist scriptures.

sentences.zh: 周武帝平齊之後，巋來賀，帝享之甚歡。

translations.literal: After Emperor Wu of Zhou pacified Qi, Kui came to offer congratulations; the emperor entertained him with great pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wu of Zhou conquered Northern Qi, Kui came to offer congratulations and was received with great warmth.

sentences.zh: 親彈琵琶，令巋起舞，巋曰：「陛下親禦五糸玄，臣敢不同百獸！

translations.literal: The emperor personally played the pipa and ordered Kui to dance. Kui said, 'Your Majesty personally handles the five-stringed dark lute—how dare your servant not join the hundred beasts!'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor played the pipa himself and asked Kui to dance. Kui said, 'Your Majesty plays the five-stringed lute himself—how can I, your servant, not join in like the beasts at court!'

sentences.zh: 」高祖受禪，恩禮彌厚，遣使賜金五百兩，銀千兩，布帛萬匹，馬五百匹。

translations.literal: ' When Emperor Gaozu received the abdication, favor and ritual courtesies grew still thicker; he sent envoys granting five hundred liang of gold, one thousand liang of silver, ten thousand bolts of cloth and silk, and five hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, his favor toward Kui grew even greater. He sent envoys with five hundred liang of gold, one thousand liang of silver, ten thousand bolts of cloth and silk, and five hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 巋來朝，上甚敬焉，詔巋位在王公之上。

translations.literal: Kui came to court; the emperor greatly respected him and ordered that Kui's rank be above kings and dukes.
translations.idiomatic: When Kui came to court, the emperor treated him with great respect and ordered that he rank above kings and dukes.

sentences.zh: 巋被服端麗，進退閒雅，天子矚目，百僚傾慕。

translations.literal: Kui's dress and adornment were dignified and beautiful; his advancing and retreating were leisurely and elegant—the Son of Heaven fixed his gaze on him, and the hundred officials looked on with admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Kui dressed with elegance and moved with grace. The emperor watched him closely, and the officials admired him.

sentences.zh: 賞賜以億計。

translations.literal: Rewards and gifts were reckoned in the hundreds of millions.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards to him were reckoned in the tens of millions.

sentences.zh: 月餘歸籓，帝親餞于滻水之上。

translations.literal: After more than a month he returned to his fief; the emperor personally saw him off on the banks of the Ba River.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month he returned to his domain, and the emperor personally saw him off on the banks of the Ba River.

sentences.zh: 後備禮納其女為晉王妃，又欲以其子瑒尚蘭陵公主。

translations.literal: Later, with full ritual propriety, his daughter was taken in marriage as Princess of Jin; the emperor also wished to marry his son Yang to Princess Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: Later his daughter was married with full ceremony to the Prince of Jin, and the emperor also wished to marry Kui's son Yang to Princess Lanling.

sentences.zh: 由是漸見親待。

translations.literal: From this he gradually came to be treated with intimacy and favor.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he was increasingly treated as a close kinsman.

sentences.zh: 獻皇后言于上曰：「梁主通家，腹心所寄，何勞猜防也。

translations.literal: Empress Xian spoke to the emperor, saying, 'The Lord of Liang is family by marriage, one in whom the heart is entrusted—why trouble to suspect and guard against him?'
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xian told the emperor, 'The Lord of Liang is family by marriage, a man in whom you may place your trust—why suspect and guard against him?'

sentences.zh: 」上然之，於是罷江陵總管，巋專制其國。

translations.literal: ' The emperor approved; thereupon the Governor-General of Jiangling was abolished, and Kui held sole rule over his state.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, abolished the Governor-General at Jiangling, and let Kui rule his state on his own.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，巋又來朝，賜縑萬匹，珍玩稱是。

translations.literal: After more than a year Kui came to court again and was granted ten thousand bolts of fine silk and rare curios in like measure.
translations.idiomatic: A year later Kui came to court again and received ten thousand bolts of fine silk and rare treasures in equal abundance.

sentences.zh: 及還，上親執手曰：「梁主久滯荊楚，未復舊都，故鄉之念，良軫懷抱。

translations.literal: When he returned, the emperor personally took his hand and said, 'The Lord of Liang has long been detained in Jing and Chu and has not recovered his old capital—the thought of home truly pierces the heart.'
translations.idiomatic: When he departed, the emperor took his hand and said, 'You have long been kept in Jing and Chu and have not regained your old capital. I know how deeply you must long for home.'

sentences.zh: 朕當振旅長江，相送旋反耳。

translations.literal: I shall raise troops on the Yangzi and see you safely returned.'
translations.idiomatic: I shall march on the Yangzi and see you safely home.'

sentences.zh: 」巋拜謝而去。

translations.literal: ' Kui bowed in thanks and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Kui bowed in thanks and left.

sentences.zh: 其年五月，寢疾，臨終上表曰：「臣以庸暗，曲荷天慈，寵冠外籓，恩逾連山，爰及子女，尚主婚王。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of that year he took to his bed with illness and on his deathbed submitted a memorial saying, 'Your servant, being mediocre and dim, has undeservedly received Heaven's kindness, favor surpassing all outer fiefs, grace exceeding linked mountains, extending even to my sons and daughters, who married princesses and kings.'
translations.idiomatic: That fifth month he fell ill. On his deathbed he submitted a memorial: 'Your servant, though mediocre and unworthy, has received Heaven's grace beyond measure, favor surpassing all outer lords, kindness as vast as mountains, extending even to my children, who have married princesses and princes.'

sentences.zh: 每願躬擐甲胄，身先士卒，掃蕩逋寇，上報明時。

translations.literal: 'Each day I wished to don armor myself, take the lead before the soldiers, sweep away fleeing bandits, and repay the enlightened age above.'
translations.idiomatic: I had hoped to don armor myself, lead the troops in person, sweep away the rebels, and repay your enlightened reign.'

sentences.zh: 而攝生乖舛，遽罹屙疾，屬纊在辰，顧陰待謝。

translations.literal: 'Yet in nurturing life I went awry and suddenly met with wasting illness; the silk wadding is placed at the hour, and I look toward shade awaiting departure.'
translations.idiomatic: But I failed in caring for my health and have suddenly fallen gravely ill. Death is near, and I await the end.'

sentences.zh: 長違聖世，感戀嗚咽，遺嗣孤藐，特乞降慈。

translations.literal: 'To part long from the sage age, moved and attached, I sob and weep; the orphaned heirs left behind are young and small—I especially beg for descending kindness.'
translations.idiomatic: To leave your sage reign fills me with grief. My orphaned heirs are young and helpless, and I beg your mercy for them.'

sentences.zh: 伏願聖躬與山嶽同固，皇基等天日俱永，臣雖九泉，實無遣恨。

translations.literal: 'Prostrate, I wish that Your Sage Person may be as firm as mountains and hills, the imperial foundation as enduring as Heaven and sun together—though your servant reaches the nine springs, truly there will be no regret left behind.'
translations.idiomatic: I pray that Your Majesty's person may be as firm as the mountains, that the imperial foundation may endure as long as Heaven and sun, and that though I go to the grave, I shall have no regret.'

sentences.zh: 」並獻所服金裝劍，上覽而嗟悼焉。

translations.literal: ' He also presented the gold-mounted sword he had worn; the emperor read it and sighed in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He also presented the gold-mounted sword he had worn. The emperor read the memorial and mourned him deeply.

sentences.zh: 巋在位二十三年，年四十四薨，梁之臣子諡曰孝明皇帝，廟號世宗。

translations.literal: Kui reigned twenty-three years and died at age forty-four; Liang's ministers and sons gave him the posthumous title Emperor Xiaoming and the temple name Shizong.
translations.idiomatic: Kui had reigned twenty-three years and died at forty-four. Liang ministers gave him the posthumous title Emperor Xiaoming and the temple name Shizong.

sentences.zh: 子琮嗣。

translations.literal: His son Cong inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Cong succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 巋著《孝經》、《周易義記》及《大小乘幽微》十四卷，行於世。

translations.literal: Kui authored the Classic of Filial Piety, Records of the Meaning of the Book of Changes, and Subtleties of the Greater and Lesser Vehicles in fourteen scrolls, which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Kui wrote the Classic of Filial Piety, Records of the Meaning of the Book of Changes, and Subtleties of the Greater and Lesser Vehicles in fourteen scrolls, all of which circulated.

sentences.zh: 琮字溫文，性寬仁，有大度，倜儻不羈，博學有文義。

translations.literal: Cong, styled Wenwen, was by nature generous and benevolent, possessed great breadth of mind, was free-spirited and unrestrained, and was broadly learned with literary understanding.
translations.idiomatic: Cong, styled Wenwen, was generous and magnanimous, free-spirited and unrestrained, broadly learned, and skilled in letters.

sentences.zh: 兼善弓馬，遣人伏地著帖，琮馳馬射之，十發十中，持帖者亦不懼。

translations.literal: He was also skilled in bow and horse; he had a man lie prone on the ground with a target affixed, Cong galloped on horseback and shot at it—ten shots, ten hits—and the man holding the target was not afraid.
translations.idiomatic: He was also skilled with bow and horse. He had a man lie prone with a target on his back, then galloped and shot—ten arrows, ten hits—while the man holding the target showed no fear.

sentences.zh: 初封東陽王，尋立為梁太子。

translations.literal: He was at first enfeoffed as Prince of Dongyang and soon established as Liang crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: He was first made Prince of Dongyang and soon afterward named Liang crown prince.

sentences.zh: 及嗣位，上賜璽書曰：「負荷堂構，其事甚重，雖窮憂勞，常須自力。

translations.literal: When he succeeded to the throne, the emperor granted him an imperial letter saying, 'Bearing the hall and framework is a matter of great weight; though exhausted with worry and toil, you must constantly rely on your own strength.'
translations.idiomatic: When he succeeded, the emperor sent him an imperial letter: 'To bear the weight of rule is a grave matter. Though worn with care and labor, you must always rely on your own strength.'

sentences.zh: 輯諧內外，親任才良，聿遵世業，是所望也。

translations.literal: 'Harmonize inner and outer, personally employ the talented and good, and diligently follow the enterprise of the age—this is what is hoped for.'
translations.idiomatic: Harmonize within and without, employ the worthy, and carry on your father's work—this is what I expect of you.'

sentences.zh: 彼之疆守，咫尺陳人，水潦之時，特宜警備。

translations.literal: 'Their frontier garrisons are but a foot away from Chen people; at times of flood and rain, special vigilance and preparation are fitting.'
translations.idiomatic: Your frontier lies close to Chen territory. In seasons of flood and rain, be especially vigilant.'

sentences.zh: 陳氏比日雖複朝聘相尋，疆埸之間猶未清肅，唯當恃我必不可幹，勿得輕人而不設備。

translations.literal: 'The Chen clan lately, though embassies and visits follow one another again, between the border marches things are still not clear and settled—you must rely on me as certainly inviolable, and must not treat others lightly and fail to make preparations.'
translations.idiomatic: Though Chen has lately resumed embassies, the border is not yet secure. Trust that I cannot be challenged, but do not underestimate them or neglect your defenses.'

sentences.zh: 朕與梁國，積世相知，重以親姻，情義彌厚。

translations.literal: 'I and the state of Liang have known each other through accumulated generations; redoubled by marriage kinship, feeling and righteousness grow ever thicker.'
translations.idiomatic: I and the state of Liang have known each other for generations, and our bond of marriage has made that tie still deeper.'

sentences.zh: 江陵之地，朝寄非輕，為國為民，深宜抑割，恆加饘粥，以禮自存。

translations.literal: 'The land of Jiangling is no light charge from the court; for the state and for the people you should deeply restrain and cut back, constantly add gruel and porridge, and preserve yourself by ritual propriety.'
translations.idiomatic: Jiangling is no light charge from the court. For the sake of state and people, restrain yourself, live simply, and preserve yourself through proper conduct.'

sentences.zh: 」又賜梁之大臣璽書，誠勉之。

translations.literal: ' He also granted imperial letters to Liang's great ministers, sincerely exhorting them.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent imperial letters to Liang's chief ministers, earnestly exhorting them.

sentences.zh: 時琮年號廣運，有識者曰：「運之為字，軍走也，吾君將奔走乎？

translations.literal: At that time Cong's era name was Guangyun; men of insight said, 'The character yun means army fleeing—will our lord take to flight?'
translations.idiomatic: Cong's era name was Guangyun. Men of insight said, 'The character yun means an army in flight—will our lord be put to flight?'

sentences.zh: 」其年，琮遣大將軍戚昕以舟師襲陳公安，不克而還。

translations.literal: ' That year Cong sent the Grand General Qi Xin with a naval force to raid Chen's Gong'an but failed to take it and returned.
translations.idiomatic: That year Cong sent Grand General Qi Xin with a fleet to raid Chen's Gong'an but failed and returned.

sentences.zh: 征琮叔父岑入朝，拜為大將軍，封懷義公，因留不遣。

translations.literal: Cong's uncle Cen was summoned to court, appointed Grand General, enfeoffed as Duke of Huaiyi, and then detained and not sent back.
translations.idiomatic: Cong's uncle Cen was summoned to court, made Grand General and Duke of Huaiyi, and then detained.

sentences.zh: 複置江陵總管以監之。

translations.literal: The Governor-General of Jiangling was re-established to supervise him.
translations.idiomatic: The Governor-General at Jiangling was re-established to supervise him.

sentences.zh: 琮所署大將軍許世武密以城召陳將宜黃侯陳紀，謀泄，琮誅之。

translations.literal: The Grand General Xu Shiwu, whom Cong had appointed, secretly invited the Chen general the Marquis of Yihuang, Chen Ji, to take the city; the plot leaked out and Cong executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Xu Shiwu, whom Cong had appointed, secretly invited the Chen general Marquis Chen Ji of Yihuang to seize the city. When the plot was exposed, Cong had him executed.

sentences.zh: 後二歲，上征琮入朝，率其臣下二百余人朝于京師，江陵父老莫不隕涕相謂曰：「吾君其不反矣！

translations.literal: Two years later the emperor summoned Cong to court; leading more than two hundred ministers and subordinates he paid court at the capital. The elders of Jiangling all shed tears and said to one another, 'Our lord surely will not return!'
translations.idiomatic: Two years later the emperor summoned Cong to court. He came with more than two hundred officials, and the elders of Jiangling wept and said to one another, 'Our lord will not return!'

sentences.zh: 」上以琮來朝，遣武鄉公崔弘度將兵戍之。

translations.literal: ' Because Cong had come to court, the emperor sent the Duke of Wuxiang, Cui Hongdu, to lead troops to garrison the place.
translations.idiomatic: Because Cong had come to court, the emperor sent Duke Cui Hongdu of Wuxiang with troops to take control.

sentences.zh: 軍至鄀州，琮叔父岩及弟瓛等懼弘度掩襲之，遂引陳人至城下，虜居民而叛，於是廢梁國。

translations.literal: When the army reached Ezhou, Cong's uncle Yan and younger brother Huan and others, fearing that Hongdu would launch a surprise attack, thereupon brought Chen men to below the walls, seized the inhabitants, and rebelled; thereupon the state of Liang was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Ezhou, Cong's uncle Yan and his brother Huan, fearing a surprise attack, brought Chen forces to the walls, seized the populace, and rebelled. The state of Liang was then abolished.

sentences.zh: 上遣左僕射高熲安集之，曲赦江陵死罪，給民複十年。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Left Vice Director Gao Jiong to pacify and settle the region, granted a special pardon for capital crimes in Jiangling, and gave the people tax exemption for ten years.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Left Vice Director Gao Jiong to pacify the region, granted a special pardon for capital crimes in Jiangling, and gave the people ten years of tax relief.

sentences.zh: 梁二主各給守墓十戶。

translations.literal: Each of the two Liang rulers was given ten households to guard their tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Each of the two Liang rulers was given ten households to tend their tombs.

sentences.zh: 拜琮為柱國，賜爵莒國公。

translations.literal: Cong was appointed Pillar of the State and granted the title Duke of Ju state.
translations.idiomatic: Cong was made Pillar of the State and Duke of Ju.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，以皇后之故，甚見親重。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, because of the empress he was greatly treated with intimacy and weight.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, Cong was greatly favored because of the empress.

sentences.zh: 拜內史令，改封梁公。

translations.literal: He was appointed Director of the Palace Secretariat and his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Director of the Palace Secretariat and enfeoffed as Duke of Liang.

sentences.zh: 琮之宗族，緦麻以上，並隨才擢用，於是諸蕭昆弟布列朝廷。

translations.literal: Cong's clan kin of mourning-grade sima and above were all promoted according to talent; thereupon the various Xiao brothers were arrayed throughout the court.
translations.idiomatic: All of Cong's clan within the mourning circle were promoted according to ability, and Xiao kinsmen filled the court.

sentences.zh: 琮性淡雅，不以職務自嬰，退朝縱酒而已。

translations.literal: Cong's nature was light and refined; he did not burden himself with official duties and, after leaving court, merely indulged in wine.
translations.idiomatic: Cong was by nature detached and easygoing. He did not burden himself with office and, after court, merely drank his fill.

sentences.zh: 內史令楊約與琮同列，帝令約宣旨誡勵，約複以私情喻之。

translations.literal: Director of the Palace Secretariat Yang Yue was of the same rank as Cong; the emperor ordered Yue to proclaim the imperial will and admonish him, and Yue again explained it to him in private feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Director Yang Yue, Cong's equal in rank, was ordered by the emperor to admonish him, and Yue also spoke to him privately.

sentences.zh: 琮答曰：「琮若複事事，則何異於公哉！

translations.literal: Cong replied, 'If Cong again attended to every matter, how would that differ from you, sir!'
translations.idiomatic: Cong replied, 'If I attended to every matter, how would I differ from you, sir!'

sentences.zh: 」約笑而退。

translations.literal: ' Yue laughed and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Yue laughed and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 約兄素，時為尚書令，見琮嫁從父妹于鉗耳氏，因謂琮曰：「公，帝王之族，望高戚美，何乃適妹鉗耳氏乎？

translations.literal: Yue's elder brother Su was then Director of the Department of State Affairs; seeing Cong marry a younger female cousin by the father's line to the Qian'er clan, he therefore said to Cong, 'Sir, you are of an imperial clan—your repute is high and your affinal beauty great—why marry your sister to the Qian'er clan?'
translations.idiomatic: Yue's brother Su was then Director of the Department of State Affairs. Seeing Cong marry a cousin to the Qian'er clan, he said, 'You are of imperial stock, of high standing and fine marriage prospects—why give your sister to the Qian'er clan?'

sentences.zh: 」琮曰：「前已嫁妹于侯莫陳氏，此複何疑！

translations.literal: ' Cong said, 'Earlier I already married a sister to the Houmochen clan—what doubt is there about this!'
translations.idiomatic: Cong said, 'I already married one sister to the Houmochen clan—what is there to question about this!'

sentences.zh: 」素曰：「鉗耳，羌也，侯莫陳，虜也，何得相比！

translations.literal: ' Su said, 'Qian'er are Qiang; Houmochen are barbarians—how can they be compared!'
translations.idiomatic: Su said, 'The Qian'er are Qiang; the Houmochen are barbarians—how can they be compared!'

sentences.zh: 」素意以虜優羌劣。

translations.literal: ' Su's meaning was that barbarians were superior and Qiang inferior.
translations.idiomatic: Su meant that the barbarians were superior and the Qiang inferior.

sentences.zh: 琮曰：「以羌異虜，未之前聞。

translations.literal: Cong said, 'That Qiang differ from barbarians—I have never heard of it before.'
translations.idiomatic: Cong said, 'That the Qiang differ from barbarians is something I have never heard before.'

sentences.zh: 」素慚而止。

translations.literal: ' Su, ashamed, stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Su, ashamed, said no more.

sentences.zh: 琮雖羈旅，見北間豪貴，無所降下。

translations.literal: Though Cong was a guest in exile, toward the great and noble of the north he showed no lowering or submission.
translations.idiomatic: Though Cong was an exile in the north, he bowed to none of its great nobles.

sentences.zh: 嘗與賀若弼深相友善，弼既被誅，複有童謠曰：「蕭蕭亦複起。

translations.literal: He had once been deeply friendly with He Ruo Bi; after Bi was executed, there was again a children's song saying, 'Xiao, xiao will rise again.'
translations.idiomatic: He had been close friends with He Ruo Bi. After Bi was executed, a children's song circulated: 'The Xiao clan will rise again.'

sentences.zh: 」帝由是忌之，遂廢於家，未幾而卒。

translations.literal: ' The emperor therefore grew jealous of him, had him dismissed to his home, and before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew suspicious and had him dismissed to his home. He soon died.

sentences.zh: 贈左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness of the Left.

sentences.zh: 子鉉，襄城通守。

translations.literal: His son Xian was Defender of Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xian was Defender of Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 複以琮弟子钜為梁公。

translations.literal: Cong's younger clansman Ju was again made Duke of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Cong's nephew Ju was then made Duke of Liang.

sentences.zh: 钜小名藏，煬帝甚昵之，以為千牛，與宇文皛出入宮掖，伺察內外。

translations.literal: Ju, whose childhood name was Zang, was greatly favored by Emperor Yang; he was made an attendant of the Thousand-Ox Guard and, with Yuwen Xiao, went in and out of the inner palace, observing and inspecting inner and outer affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Ju, childhood name Zang, was greatly favored by Emperor Yang. He was made an attendant of the Thousand-Ox Guard and, with Yuwen Xiao, moved freely through the inner palace, watching affairs within and without.

sentences.zh: 帝每有遊宴，钜未嘗不從焉，遂于宮中多行淫穢。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor held excursions and banquets, Ju never failed to follow; he thereupon committed many lewd and filthy acts within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: He never missed the emperor's feasts and excursions, and committed many lewd acts within the palace.

sentences.zh: 江都之變，為宇文化及所殺。

translations.literal: At the Jiangdu upheaval he was killed by Yuwen Huaji.
translations.idiomatic: At the Jiangdu upheaval he was killed by Yuwen Huaji.

sentences.zh: 瓛字欽文，少聰敏，解屬文。

translations.literal: Huan, styled Qinwen, was from youth clever and keen and skilled in composing literary pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Huan, styled Qinwen, was clever from youth and skilled at composition.

sentences.zh: 在梁為荊州刺史，頗有能名。

translations.literal: In Liang he was Governor of Jing province and had a considerable reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: In Liang he was Governor of Jing province and enjoyed a reputation for ability.

sentences.zh: 崔弘度以兵至若阝州，瓛懼，與其叔父岩奔于陳。

translations.literal: When Cui Hongdu came with troops to Ruozhou, Huan was afraid; with his uncle Yan he fled to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Hongdu advanced on Ruozhou with troops, Huan fled with his uncle Yan to Chen.

sentences.zh: 陳主以為侍中、安東將軍、吳州刺史，甚得物情，三吳父老皆曰：「瓛吾君子也。

translations.literal: The Chen ruler made him Palace Attendant, General Who Pacifies the East, and Governor of Wu province; he won men's hearts greatly, and the elders of the Three Wu all said, 'Huan is our gentleman.'
translations.idiomatic: The Chen ruler made him Palace Attendant, General Who Pacifies the East, and Governor of Wu province. He won great popular favor, and the elders of the Three Wu said, 'Huan is our true leader.'

sentences.zh: 」及陳亡，吳人推瓛為主。

translations.literal: ' When Chen perished, the people of Wu urged Huan as their leader.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen fell, the people of Wu urged Huan to lead them.

sentences.zh: 吳人見梁武、簡文及詧、巋等兄弟並第三而踐尊位，瓛自以巋之第三子也，深自矜負。

translations.literal: The people of Wu saw that Liang Wudi, Jianwendi, and the brothers Cha and Kui were all third sons who ascended the honored position; Huan, considering himself Kui's third son, deeply prided himself on this.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Wu noted that Liang Wudi, Jianwendi, and the brothers Cha and Kui had all been third sons who rose to the throne. Huan, as Kui's third son, took great pride in this.

sentences.zh: 有謝異者，頗知廢興，梁、陳之際，言無不驗，江南人甚敬信之。

translations.literal: There was one Xie Yi who was quite knowledgeable about rise and fall; in the interval between Liang and Chen, nothing he said failed to come true, and the people of Jiangnan greatly revered and trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: A man named Xie Yi was skilled at reading the rise and fall of states. During the Liang and Chen transition, his predictions always came true, and the people of the south greatly revered him.

sentences.zh: 及陳主被擒，異奔於瓛，由是益為眾所歸。

translations.literal: When the Chen ruler was captured, Yi fled to Huan; from this he was still more followed by the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chen ruler was captured, Yi fled to Huan, and Huan gained still more followers.

sentences.zh: 褒國公宇文述以兵討之，瓛遣王哀守吳州，自將拒述。

translations.literal: Duke of Baoguo, Yuwen Shu, came with troops to suppress him; Huan sent Wang Ai to guard Wu province and personally led the army to resist Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Yuwen Shu of Baoguo marched against him. Huan sent Wang Ai to hold Wu province and led the army himself to resist Shu.

sentences.zh: 述遣兵別道襲吳州，哀懼，衣道士服，棄城而遁。

translations.literal: Shu sent troops by a separate route to strike Wu province; Ai was afraid, put on Daoist robes, abandoned the city, and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Shu sent troops by another route to strike Wu province. Ai, terrified, dressed as a Daoist priest and abandoned the city.

sentences.zh: 瓛眾聞之，悉無鬥志，與述一戰而敗。

translations.literal: When Huan's host heard of it, all lost fighting spirit; after one battle with Shu they were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan's troops heard this, they lost all fighting spirit and were defeated in a single battle.

sentences.zh: 瓛將左右數人逃於太湖，匿於民家，為人所執，送於述所，斬之長安，時年二十一。

translations.literal: Huan took a few men at his left and right and fled to Lake Tai, hiding in a commoner's house; he was seized by someone, sent to Shu's place, and beheaded at Chang'an—he was then twenty-one years old.
translations.idiomatic: Huan fled with a few followers to Lake Tai and hid in a commoner's house, but was captured and sent to Shu. He was beheaded at Chang'an at the age of twenty-one.

sentences.zh: 弟璟，為朝請大夫、尚衣奉禦。

translations.literal: His younger brother Jing was a Grand Master for Palace Attendance and Attendant of the Imperial Wardrobe.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Jing was Grand Master for Palace Attendance and Attendant of the Imperial Wardrobe.

sentences.zh: 瑒，曆衛尉卿、秘書監、陶丘侯。

translations.literal: Yang successively held the offices of Commandant of the Guards, Director of the Palace Library, and Marquis of Taoqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Yang served as Commandant of the Guards, Director of the Palace Library, and Marquis of Taoqiu.

sentences.zh: 瑀，曆內史侍郎、河池太守。

translations.literal: Yu successively held the offices of Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat and Administrator of Hechi.
translations.idiomatic: Yu served as Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat and Administrator of Hechi.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：三五哲王，防深慮遠，舅甥之國，罕執鈞衡，母后之家，無聞傾敗。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: The sage kings of the Three and Five eras guarded deeply and thought far; states of maternal uncles and nephews rarely held the balance of power, and the houses of empresses' kin were unheard of in ruin and overthrow.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer remarks: The sage kings of antiquity guarded against danger with foresight. States ruled by maternal uncles and nephews rarely held real power, and empresses' kin were seldom heard of in ruin.

sentences.zh: 爰及漢、晉，顛覆繼軌，皆由乎進不以禮，故其斃亦速。

translations.literal: Extending to Han and Jin, overthrow followed in the tracks of predecessors—all because advancement was not by ritual propriety, and therefore their destruction was also swift.
translations.idiomatic: Down through Han and Jin, ruin followed ruin, all because advancement came without proper restraint—and so their fall was swift as well.

sentences.zh: 若使獨孤權侔呂、霍，必敗于仁壽之前，蕭氏勢均梁、竇，豈全于大業之後！

translations.literal: If the Dugu clan's power had matched the Lü and Huo, they would surely have been defeated before the Renshou era; if the Xiao clan's momentum had equaled the Liang and Dou, how could they have been preserved whole after the Daye era!
translations.idiomatic: Had the Dugu clan's power rivaled that of the Lü and Huo, they would surely have fallen before the Renshou era. Had the Xiao clan's influence matched that of the Liang and Dou, how could they have survived intact after the Daye reign!

sentences.zh: 今或不隕舊基，或更隆先構，豈非處之以道，不預權寵之所致乎！

translations.literal: Now, whether some did not fall from their old foundations or others still further exalted their ancestors' structures—is this not caused by being placed according to the Way and not participating in power and favor!
translations.idiomatic: That some did not fall from their old standing while others rose even higher than their forebears—was this not because they were governed by principle and kept from sharing in power and privilege!
